title: Microsoft Teams: pop out calls into a separate window in the browser
summary: Hold: the briefing presents October as the actual launch month, but the sources give a target and expected rollout dates, not confirmation of the launch month. It also overstates when the window appears and understates the published product-level Teams licensing requirement.

claims.claim: Teams browser app users can pop out calls into a simplified separate call window.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams browser app users will be able to pop out calls into a simplified call window

claims.claim: The simplified call window stays available while users navigate away from the hosting tab or PWA.
claims.quote: a simplified call window that stays available while they navigate away from, hide, or minimize the tab or progressive web app (PWA) hosting the call.

claims.claim: The simplified call window stays available while users hide the hosting tab or PWA.
claims.quote: a simplified call window that stays available while they navigate away from, hide, or minimize the tab or progressive web app (PWA) hosting the call.

claims.claim: The simplified call window stays available while users minimise the hosting tab or PWA.
claims.quote: a simplified call window that stays available while they navigate away from, hide, or minimize the tab or progressive web app (PWA) hosting the call.

claims.quote: We are introducing a new Call Monitor experience in Microsoft Teams for Web that helps users stay connected to meetings while working in other browser tabs.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The experience reaches its intended users without an administrator enabling it, so defaultState is on.
claims.quote: Users will receive the new Picture-in-Picture (PiP) Call Monitor experience during Teams meetings. ... No admin action is required before rollout.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: MC1462921 requires no admin action or setting change before rollout.
claims.quote: No admin action is required before rollout.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no documentation page for this specific Teams for Web Call Monitor feature at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "web" "Call Monitor" "Picture-in-Picture"; read limits-specifications-teams and meeting-policies-overview. Results described VDI Call Monitor and Azure Communication Services mobile PiP, not this feature.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No dedicated admin UI setting or automation operation for the Teams for Web call pop-out/PiP Call Monitor is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams web Call Monitor Picture-in-Picture admin setting disable Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; "Teams" browser "pop out" disable admin policy. Read meeting-policies-overview; searched Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy for picture, PiP, pop-out, monitor and browser: no matches.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap record and MC1462921 do not name a licence, meter or charge for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete roadmap record and supplied MC1462921 notice for licence/license, meter, pricing and charge; neither contains a licensing or charging requirement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no licence specific to the call window is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing notes and the corresponding Cost and licensing sentence with: 'Microsoft Learn says that, except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in the organisation must have a Teams license before using Teams. No licence or meter specific to this call window is published at the time of writing (November 2026).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Replace the licensing open question with 'Will Microsoft publish any licence requirement specific to this call window? Watch the Teams licensing pages.'

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; changes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no separate licence or meter specific to this call window.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams web Picture-in-Picture Call Monitor license pricing meter; Microsoft Teams license required users Teams web licensing options. Read user-access and limits-specifications-teams; pricing results describe general Teams client usage, not a separate window entitlement or meter.

claims.claim: Neither supplied record describes whether the window shows participant names, video or shared content beyond controls.
claims.quote: Searched: read full MC1462921 and roadmap description for participant names, video and shared content. The notice specifies 'key meeting controls'; the roadmap specifies a 'simplified call window', without describing that other content.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Neither supplied record describes new permissions, sign-in, identity behaviour or new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: read full MC1462921 and roadmap description for permissions, sign-in, identity and data access. They describe the call window and meeting controls but no changes in those areas.

claims.claim: MC1462921 says no compliance considerations were identified.
claims.quote: No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

claims.claim: Neither supplied record describes an agent or automated action beyond the user-facing call window.
claims.quote: Searched: read full MC1462921 and roadmap description for agents and automated actions. The descriptions concern users multitasking in an existing call or meeting and a separate window for meeting controls.

claims.claim: MC1462921 recommends confirming users run supported browser versions for Teams for Web.
claims.quote: Confirm that users are running supported browser versions for Teams for Web.

claims.claim: MC1462921 recommends reviewing Teams for Web prerequisites and supported browsers in Learn.

claims.claim: Teams meeting policy documentation describes policies controlling features available to meeting organisers and participants.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can use meeting and events policies to control the features that are available to organizers and participants of meetings and events in your organization.

claims.claim: The meeting policy documentation does not list this call window among its controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams web Call Monitor Picture-in-Picture admin setting disable Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. Read meeting-policies-overview in full and searched the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference for picture, PiP, pop-out, monitor and browser; neither documents this window.

claims.claim: The feature actually launched in October 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "569206" "October 2026" launched Call Monitor; read roadmap record and MC1462921. The record gives Launched plus an October target; the notice gives expected October rollout completion, not confirmed actual launch timing.
claims.fix: Replace 'Launched in October 2026' in the summary and change note with 'The roadmap status is Launched, with an October CY2026 target'. Keep the notice's rollout dates explicitly described as scheduled starts and expected completion dates.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users will see a call window appear when they leave the active call tab.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "web" "Call Monitor" "Picture-in-Picture"; read MC1462921 and roadmap description. The notice says Teams 'can display' meeting controls; the roadmap says users 'will be able to pop out calls', not that leaving the tab always opens a window.
claims.fix: Replace 'Teams for web users in your tenant will see a new window during calls as they work in other tabs' with 'Teams can display meeting controls in a separate PiP window when users move away from the active meeting tab'. Replace 'Users will see a window appear when they leave the call tab' with 'Teams can display the window when users leave the active meeting tab'. In the impact rationale, replace the sentence with 'Teams for web meeting participants in supported browsers can receive a separate window containing meeting controls when they switch tabs, so support staff may get questions.'
